items.prompt: Me lavo ___ manos antes de comer.
items.explanation: With parts of the body, Spanish uses the article, not the possessive: las manos.
optionNotes: With body parts, use the article: me already says whose hands.
Unas is indefinite; you mean your own hands.

items.explanation: A cold: estoy resfriado, or estoy resfriada for a woman (also: tengo un resfriado).
optionNotes: A state of health takes estar, not ser.
Un frío is a word-for-word translation; a cold is un resfriado.

items.prompt: Hoy mi hermana ___ muy nerviosa: tiene un examen.
items.explanation: How someone feels at the moment takes estar.
optionNotes: Es nerviosa would describe her character, not how she feels today.
Tener does not go with nerviosa.
Hacer does not go with nerviosa.

items.explanation: Embarazada is a false friend: it means “pregnant”. “I'm embarrassed” is me da vergüenza.
optionNotes: This is the false friend: embarazada does not mean “embarrassed”.
Angry is enfadada (Spain) or enojada (Latin America).
